conviction_note: The evidence is close to balanced. On the positive side are the peer margin read-across from First Hawaiian (FHB), a September Fed hike that management's year-end margin path already assumed, and a stock that has fallen about 8 points behind KRE since the Q2 print with 8.8% of float short. On the negative side are a guidance-based build that lands slightly under the $202M revenue consensus, which this name punished last quarter (-4.7%), and FHB's CRE charge-off. The findings sum to +0.9; the scaled number is (2x0.52-1)x5.0 = +0.2 because nothing here is a company-level number the market has not seen.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $1.52 and revenue $202.3M (Benzinga snapshot 2026-10-02, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BOH/earnings-forecasts, as reported in search results; the page itself returned 403). Earnings Whispers lists $1.54 (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026 / https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/BOH) and AAII lists $1.53 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/520346-what-you-need-to-know-about-bank-of-hawaii-corporations-q3-earnings), so three sources agree on $1.52-1.54. The company's own Q2 call guide (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026): margin up about 5bp a quarter to about 2.90% by year-end, assuming one hike in mid-September; Q3 fees about $43M normalized; Q3 expenses about $112.5M; deposit costs 1.25-1.30%; 10-15% of about $2B of public deposits running off in Q3; buybacks of $20M in Q3. My build from that guide: margin about 2.84%, net interest income about $157.5M, revenue about $200.5M (-0.9% against the revenue bar), EPS about $1.51-1.52 (in line). The revenue bar is less certain: Q2 revenue is quoted as $196.9M and as $198.3M by different aggregators.
positioning_check: Short interest is 3.5M shares, 8.78% of float, 6.2 days to cover, as of 2026-08-19 (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/boh/shortinterest). Curvedtrading's FINRA series has 12.0 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 settlement against 6.2 on 2026-07-31 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/boh/short-interest/, snippet only, page 403). No October settlement was found. That is elevated for a bank but not crowded in the 18-23% sense. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline. Put/call open interest is 1.83, but total open interest is only 252 contracts and the ATM spread is 63% of mid, so the option market makes no usable directional statement. The event-implied move is 5.65% and only indicative. Tape: BOH closed $80.02 on 2026-07-27 and trades at $70.55 intraday on 2026-10-23, -11.8%; KRE fell from $75.52 to $72.53 over the same period, -4.0% (Yahoo chart v8, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BOH?range=6mo&interval=1d and https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/KRE?range=3mo&interval=1d). Over the last 5 days BOH is up +5.1% against KRE +3.9%. Argus cut its target to $66 on 2026-09-30 and Piper Sandler cut from $85 to $78 (Neutral) around 2026-10-01.

findings.finding: First Hawaiian (FHB), BOH's only same-market peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-23. Its margin rose 5bp to 3.30%, above its own Q2-call outlook of about 3.27%. Its interest-bearing deposit cost FELL 3bp to 1.72% even though the Fed hiked mid-quarter, and total deposits grew $50M to $20.2B, so Hawaii deposit pricing did not reprice up after the hike. BOH guided about +5bp a quarter (2.78% to about 2.83-2.84%) with deposit costs of 1.25-1.30%; if FHB's pattern carries over, BOH's Q3 margin and net interest income land at the top of that path or above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-27 net interest income came in at $153.6M against about $156.7M expected, EPS was in line ($1.47 vs $1.46), and the stock fell -4.7% (baseline). BOH trades on the net interest income line.
findings.why_not_priced: FHB printed this morning, after BOH's estimates were set (consensus snapshot 2026-10-02). FHB's stock fell about -3.5% today on its credit line (25.225 vs 26.13), so the tape is not rewarding the margin read-across. If it were priced, BOH estimates would have moved up and BOH would have outperformed KRE by more than its +0.3% intraday today.
findings.independence: This is a peer proxy, not BOH's own number. BOH's balance sheet is different: a lower margin, a 58% fixed-to-float mix and $1.4B of pay-fixed swaps. Management's own statement that a hike helps net interest income at first points the same way (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026). The FHB credit finding below shares the same document.

findings.finding: FHB took a $20.3M provision in Q3 (Q2: $5.6M), driven by a $12.5M partial charge-off on a single CRE loan plus other CRE downgrades. Net charge-offs were 0.60% annualized (Q2: 0.11%) and nonperforming assets rose to $46.0M from $39.5M. BOH's own criticized assets rose to 2.81% from 2.12% in Q2 because of one borrower (93% real-estate secured, about 58% weighted LTV). A charge-off or migration on that BOH credit in Q3 would cost provision against a consensus that assumes about $3-4M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BOH's credit line has been quiet: NCOs of 0.03-0.10% and NPAs of 8bp in 2026, and no recent print turned on credit. FHB fell about -3.5% on 2026-10-23 on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: BOH rose slightly on FHB's print day, so the market did not carry FHB's credit hit over to BOH. If it had, BOH would be down with FHB today. BOH's single-borrower criticized increase from Q2 is disclosed but its Q3 resolution is not.
findings.independence: BOH's Q2 call disclosed the criticized-asset rise from one borrower (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026). Shares the FHB 8-K with the margin finding above. It is one CRE loan at a different bank, so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: Two hurricanes hit Hawaii in Q3. Lala (2026-08-14) closed BOH branches on Hawai'i Island and Maui; Lowell (2026-09-07/08) closed all BOH branches on Kaua'i. August 2026 visitor arrivals fell -5.6% y/y and visitor spending -9.7% (DBEDT preliminary). The quarter could carry a qualitative reserve build, deferrals or softer card and fee activity, and the call will be asked about Hawaii's outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior BOH print that turned on a weather event in the baseline window. The April 2026 Kona-low storms preceded a -0.04% reaction (2026-04-20).
findings.why_not_priced: The storms are public. No BOH relief or deferral program for Lala or Lowell was found, and FHB's release did not mention the storms; its allowance ratio fell to 1.14% from 1.15%. That argues the transmission is small, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Visitor data: https://mauinow.com/?p=539526 and https://centreforaviation.com/news/hawaii-records-772000-visitor-arrivals-in-aug-2026-1374086. Lala branch closure: https://www.boh.com/newsroom/bank-of-hawaii-to-temporarily-close-branches-on-hawaii-island-and-maui-county-due-to-hurricane-lala. This is macro-to-company transmission that neither BOH nor FHB has confirmed.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, and the September dot plot implies one more hike in 2026. BOH's year-end margin target of about 2.90% was explicitly conditional on that September hike, and management said hikes help net interest income at first, with a 34% deposit beta. The call can reaffirm the 2.90% exit and extend the path into 2027 on a higher-for-longer curve, which would be the guidance read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The margin-path guide is what this stock trades on. The 2026-01-26 print, with margin expansion, bought +6.09%; the 2026-07-27 net interest income shortfall sold -4.7% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The hike was inside BOH's guide, so the direction is known. But BOH fell from $75.43 (2026-09-15) to $66.26 (2026-10-13) after the hike, against KRE -6.7% over the same span, so the market has been pricing the hike as a deposit-cost or AOCI risk rather than as the tailwind management described. A reaffirmed guide cuts against that.
findings.independence: Guide conditional on the hike: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026 and https://www.webull.com/news/15303749301904384. FHB's CEO says its balance sheet is 'well positioned to benefit from rising interest rates' (FHB 8-K, same document as findings 1-2).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: BOH is -11.8% since its Q2 print against KRE -4.0%, is 17.7% below its 52-week high, has 8.8% of float short with 6.2 days to cover (August), and has had two target cuts in the last month (Argus to $66 on 2026-09-30; Piper Sandler $85 to $78 around 2026-10-01). An in-line print with a reaffirmed margin path meets low expectations and a moderately heavy short book. The last 5 days, +5.1% against KRE +3.9%, show some of that has already started.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is not directly observable in the baseline. The last two prints after drawdowns were 2026-04-20 (-0.04%) and 2026-01-26 (+6.09%).
findings.why_not_priced: The relative drawdown itself is the market's statement. If the short book had covered, short interest would have fallen and BOH would have closed the gap to KRE; it has closed only about 1 point of an 8-point gap. Short-interest data is from August and may be stale.

findings.finding: The Q2-call guide builds to revenue of about $200.5M and EPS of about $1.51-1.52: margin about 2.84% on about $22.0B of average earning assets after the $200-300M public-deposit runoff, plus $43M of normalized fees, $112.5M of expenses and about $4M of provision. That is about -0.9% against the $202.3M revenue consensus and in line to -2c against the $1.52-1.54 EPS consensus. This name sold off -4.7% last quarter on exactly that pattern, a small revenue miss with in-line EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-27: revenue $198.3M against $199.7M (-0.7%), EPS in line, stock -4.7%. 2025-07-28: revenue shortfall, stock -4.29% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus revenue figure appears to sit above the company's own guided components. It may include a different revenue definition (Q2 is quoted at both $196.9M and $198.3M), which is why this is sized small and the bar is flagged as uncertain. If the market already expected a revenue shortfall, the estimate would have been cut toward about $200M by now.
findings.independence: This is my inference from guidance, not a primary number. Finding 1 (FHB margin beat) points the other way on net interest income; the two net to a roughly in-line quarter, which is why print_vs_bar_pct is -0.5.

findings.finding: BOH planned $20M of buybacks in Q3 and $20M in Q4 (from $89M of remaining authorization). At about $68 average that is about 290k shares a quarter, about 0.7% of shares, against $78 per share paid in Q2. The call may lift the pace with the stock lower.

findings.why_not_priced: The plan is inside guidance, so only an increase would matter. CET1 of 12.12% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000046195/000004619526000054/ex991earningsrelease063026.htm) gives room for one.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive against an 8-point relative drawdown, two recent target cuts and a heavy put/call open-interest ratio. Option liquidity is too thin (252 open contracts, 63% spread) to count as a strong skew, so there is no option-market statement to overrule.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission the company or a direct counterparty has not confirmed is filed small): hurricane finding cut from -0.4 to -0.2, because FHB's release did not mention the storms and its allowance ratio fell.

Lessons 3 and 7 (own caveat reaches the number; short interest checked before negatives): FHB credit read-across cut from -0.7 to -0.5, because BOH rose on FHB's print day and the short book (8.8% of float) is a mild squeeze mechanism.

Lesson 1 (reaction function): kept the revenue-build finding at -0.5, since this name sold an in-line EPS / small revenue miss -4.7% last quarter. Lesson 6: bar sourced to three agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide, so no cap applied. p_up and abs_move_pct unchanged.
